note.item: Maintenance release for 2.1.0. It updates an installed shop of 2.0.0 or later in place: Joomla runs its database changes automatically (schema 2.1.1: every Alfa Commerce table now uses one collation, utf8mb4_unicode_ci). Requirements are unchanged.

After updating: if System - Page Cache is enabled, clear Joomla's cache (System > Clear Cache), or pages cached by 2.1.0 keep their blank untranslated names; rebuild the index of a search engine so it carries the names as shown.

security.item: Tools > Security now reports hidden files (such as .htaccess or .user.ini) inside Alfa Commerce's folders; only desktop clutter (.DS_Store, ._ files, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini) is ignored.

addition.item: For plugins: onAlfaNotificationPushed (NotificationPushedEvent): one event per notification core writes, after the row is written and outside any transaction of core's, with the notification's id, key, group, severity, title, message, link and whether it was new, updated or raised again. A listener's failure is logged and never undoes the notification.

When a content language is published after the shop has content, a warning notification says how many items, categories, manufacturers and other records have no text in it yet and show the default language's, with a link to Tools > Backfill empty translations. It follows the translations as they are saved, clears itself when none is left, and once dismissed stays dismissed.

change.item: Alfa Commerce ships in English only. Other languages are separate language packs, published on alfacommerce.gr (Greek first) and offered as updates in Joomla.

Core writes its notifications directly: the Notifications admin model and its save events (onAlfaAdminBeforeSave, onAlfaAdminAfterSave, Joomla's content and table events) are no longer involved, so a plugin's message about a saved record no longer appears beside a refund answer. Notifications raised while a payment provider's word or a staff refund action holds the order are written once it has finished; one whose work is rolled back is never written.

For payment plugins: a provider word (settleRefund(), holdRefund(), releaseRefund(), refundPayment() with gateway_moved) is sent outside any database transaction of the plugin's. Sent inside one it is refused (OUTCOME_FAILED, nothing written) and is sent again outside. The official payment plugins open no transaction.

For payment plugins: the 'report_id' a provider word names is checked against the word: it must be a report of the payment's own gateway, name the same provider refund id when both carry one, and state the same figure when no id decides. Otherwise a warning is logged and the word is decided as if it named no report.
For plugins and templates: ActionRegistry::methodType() reads the row's recorded method type only; a row that records none is unknown (no type is inferred from its method any more).
Saving a record stores only what was entered for each language; empty languages stay empty (and show the default) instead of receiving copies.

Alfa generates and makes unique only an empty URL alias, and never renames one that was typed. A save that would give a record an address another record already has, in any language, is refused with a message naming that record and the language; an address two records already shared is kept and named in a warning. Save as Copy gives the copy aliases of its own.

When the site language is not a published content language, untranslated content is shown in the content language created first, and the notifications bell warns the administrators until the setting is fixed.

Documents issued in the back office, and e-mails for an order without a language of its own, are now in the site's default content language; 2.1.0 used the language of the administrator who issued or sent them.
Tools > About marks Alfa's default language and says when Joomla's site language is not a published content language.
The update converts only Alfa Commerce's own tables to the new collation. A table of another extension, or one an earlier version left, is left as it is and named once in the setup log.

A category inside an archived or trashed category is no longer offered for a new assignment, and every save (items, payment, shipping, discount, tax and item field restrictions, cart rules, the Items batch, the REST API) refuses a new assignment of an unavailable category, naming it; categories a record already holds are kept and marked "(Parent in trash)" or "(Parent archived)". A category can no longer be filed under one inside the archive or the trash.

Category pickers offer published and unpublished categories for a new choice, and keep and mark an archived or trashed category a record already holds; parent pickers never offer archived or trashed categories.
Stock locations say Enabled and Disabled everywhere: list, filter, toolbar, messages and the combination detail.
Wide administrator lists scroll inside their own box instead of moving the whole page; the notifications panel stays clear of the side menu; Cart Rules has the Notifications button.
For developers: the fail-closed options trait moved to Field/Traits (HasFailClosedOptionsTrait).
Alfa Commerce's own plugins and modules carry every language string they show in their own language files; core's language files hold only the component's strings.

The English names the calculated tax "tax" everywhere it is shown, on screen, in e-mails and on printed documents (Tax rate, Includes tax, Excl. tax, Tax %, Tax analysis, Tax amount, Tax total); "VAT" stays only for the VAT number.

fix.item: A provider's hold with no amount, under a new refund id, is no longer taken for a refund already booked without an id: it is refused until the provider's figure is given, so one provider refund is never booked twice.

A provider refund kept for staff is always kept with the mark that lists it and holds the refund block: when that mark cannot be written, nothing of the word is kept and the word is sent again; money moved beyond a refund decision on a payment set refunded by hand is now listed and blocking.

A provider refund on a payment with no recorded payment method type (an older payment) or paid with the customer's credit is now listed on the order and holds the refund block, like on every other payment.
A word repeated about a provider refund kept for staff now says that staff decide it on the payment; "staff resolved before" is said only when they did.

After a provider word's work is committed, a status change it causes that makes a plugin send another word about the same order now runs that word under the order's lock, never as part of the finished one.

Two notices raised at the same moment about the same new subject no longer make the second action fail (for example two operator orders landing in a status that is missing): they land on one notice, holding the later one's text. This holds for any number of them at once.

A payment that records no payment method type (an older payment): a provider refund it holds for staff can always be recorded, reconciled or resolved from its actions, also when its payment method was deleted; no plugin action is guessed for it from its method any more.

Record this refund that completes a payment's refunds now changes the order's status, sends its e-mail and calls the plugins' status-change hooks after the order is released; a Record that is rolled back sends and changes nothing.
A deadlock on the history entry of a refund the provider just made no longer lets the provider's word go on half written: the word is not kept and is sent again.
Tools > Security no longer reports a language pack's files as changes to the installation.
When the only differences are extra files, the security warning says how many extra files are not in the official release instead of saying the files have been changed.
When the official checksums cannot be verified or fetched, the security warning says so instead of saying the files have been changed.
The update removes files that earlier versions left in Alfa Commerce's folders and no longer uses, and names each one; a file whose content was changed is kept and named for you to check.

A text not yet translated now shows in the site's default language instead of blank, on every page and list (storefront, back office, API, cart, checkout, order lines and e-mails). The default language is the site language set in Joomla's Language Manager, never the language of the visitor or of the administrator.
In another language, a category's listing keeps its category and filter while only the default language has an alias, and category links cached by 2.1.0 are no longer served.
A multilingual form requires the default language's name, not the first language in Joomla's list.
Order e-mails take each status text from the default language when the order's language has none; an order without a language is written in the default language.
Search finds items by the names they show in each language.

Every Alfa table now uses one collation, utf8mb4_unicode_ci, as Joomla's tables do. Searching the order statuses in a language other than the site's default, and the REST API with ?lang=, no longer fail. The update converts 25 tables; on a large shop it takes a while.
The categories' batch "Set parent category" refuses a move that would put two categories on one address in any language, naming the category already there.

If the update cannot convert a table to the new collation (for example, two stored values that a unique key now reads as one), the update still completes, names the table, the key and the rows, and a notification stays until the cause is corrected and the package is installed again, which converts what is left.

An update interrupted before it finished (a time limit, a lost connection) is noticed on the next administrator page: a notification names the Alfa Commerce tables left in the old collation until the package is installed again.

Payment and shipping methods that allow every category, manufacturer, place, user or shipping method show an "All ..." chip; a new payment or shipping method shows "All ..." for every scope it allows.
The order screen shows the order's currency by name.
Administrator lists sort as their sort field says, on the first visit and when "ID Descending" is chosen; Usergroups too.

The storefront order-complete page shows the order number; Edit Payment shows a stored amount in the order currency's format and a refused amount exactly as it was typed; the customer profile form no longer offers Save & New or Save as Copy, and the server refuses them too.
Form markup: every label names a real control, every control has an id or name, media zones no longer share ids.
The typed confirmation accepts exactly the phrase shown.
Tools > Reset to default no longer scrolls sideways and shows each customer group's price display as readable lines.
The customer groups list no longer offers a Status filter that filtered nothing.
The order status e-mail help's example layout and banner position have readable names; the banner's default is empty.
Choice fields drawn as checkboxes, radios or buttons are announced once, by their group's name.
Long stored values (paths, keys, transaction ids, SKUs) wrap in their cells instead of widening the page; the document series list scrolls in its own box.
The filters module's Top Center and Bottom Center positions are named, the search module shows an inline SVG loading image, and the stock movements hint shows its search syntax.

Translated messages no longer show internal codes or fixed English: the update's message about the moved shipping options, the warning about a delivery destination that cannot be resolved, the message after a status change moved stock, the search index rebuild message, and the states, mismatches and reasons of the order's reconciliation panel.

The order-status e-mail is sent only after the change is saved: a status change made as part of a larger payment, shipment or order operation no longer e-mails the customer before that operation is complete or when it is undone, and a slow or unresponsive mail server no longer holds the order.
With a language pack installed, Tools > Download package (full or changed files only) no longer puts the pack's files into Alfa Commerce's package: they belong to the pack.

Tools > Download package, changed files only, now says there is nothing to download when none of the changed files belongs to the package, instead of failing with an error. Any other export failure shows one plain sentence, and the details go to the tools log.

The update from 2.1.0 removes the Greek files 2.1.0 installed, so without the Greek language pack Alfa Commerce shows English throughout. Uninstalling removes any that are left. A file whose content was changed is kept and named, and a language pack's files are never touched.
The mini-cart shows why a cart line cannot be bought in words on every page, not as a language key, when the page belongs to another component.

language.item: The update's link-table error can now be translated.
Shopper-facing choice-field errors, the combinations drag handle and several form options are translatable texts; the state words that must agree with a noun are Alfa's own texts.
The English texts say "item", never "product": the component, its guided tours, its plugins and its modules.

Corrected English texts: the search module's loading image fields, the order number token of the order e-mails, a place's parent field, the cart rule free-shipping message, the categories tour's image tab and the discounts tour's badge step; the Users and Usergroups permissions are named as their screens.

note.item: Feature release. It updates an installed shop of 2.0.0 or later in place: Joomla runs its database changes automatically (schema 2.1.0, two new tables: #__alfa_maintenance and #__alfa_refund_report_outcomes). Requirements are unchanged.

addition.item: Tools, Reset and clear, Reset to default: gives the Alfa Options back the values an installation writes, and rebuilds the price display of every customer group from them. The download store's path, the delivery destination the merchant mapped and the record of the menu items the setup created are kept. The page lists every setting that would change, current value and default, before anything is changed. No catalogue, customer, order, document, payment, stock or other business data, no file, scheduled task, guided tour or permission is touched. Requires the Tools and Configure permissions.

Tools, Reset and clear, Clear everything: a factory reset of the shop's Alfa data. Core clears core's data and each installed Alfa plugin clears its own. Core removes its own tables (the ones its installation SQL and the extensions it bundles make, and its language tables) and the objects of the store of purchased files, then makes its tables again with the installation's own SQL and steps; product images in the site's images folder are kept and counted. Afterwards Alfa Commerce is installed at the current version with no previous shop data; Joomla's record of the extension, its permissions and its enabled state stay, and new identifiers continue above the old ones. The page lists core's tables with their rows and the files with their sizes, and every installed Alfa plugin with whether it clears its own data; the run starts only after the phrase DELETE ALL ALFA DATA is typed.

Clear Data for Alfa plugins: a plugin clears the data it owns in its hook onClearData(ClearDataEvent $event): void, and reports an expected failure with $event->setError(). The hook is the whole contract: a plugin without it is shown "Automatic Clear Data not supported" and none of its data is touched; it loads and works as before. Clear everything calls every plugin's hook, enabled or not, before core's clear. A plugin that fails, throws or stops the request pauses the run with the reason and the offer to try again or continue anyway; one without support, or uninstalled during the run, is reported with a warning; none blocks the reset, which then reports "Core reset completed with extension cleanup warnings".

Tools, Extensions: the Alfa extensions installed apart from Alfa Commerce, with their type, version, state and Clear Data support. Clear Data calls one extension's hook; the extension stays installed. Remove extension only uninstalls it through Joomla and keeps its data. Remove extension and its data clears its data first and uninstalls it only when that succeeded; when it fails, the error is shown and nothing is uninstalled. A package is one row; a module can only be removed. Clear Data and Remove extension and its data take the permission to clear Alfa data and the typed phrase DELETE EXTENSION DATA; removing takes Joomla's permission to uninstall extensions. Each Clear Data is recorded in Joomla's User Actions Log and the maintenance log. An unexpected error of the screen is said in one sentence, its details in the maintenance log, never as an error page.

One installer gate for every Alfa extension (AlfaInstallerGate): the minimum Alfa Commerce version. No install, update or uninstall is ever refused because Clear everything is running, paused or did not finish. Uninstalling an Alfa plugin or package, from Joomla's Extension Manager too, says that its data stays and where it is cleared; so does uninstalling a plugin of an Alfa package on its own.
A new permission, Clear Alfa data, granted to no group: only a Super User can run Clear everything until a Super User grants it.

While Clear everything runs, Alfa Commerce is in maintenance: the storefront, the administrator screens and the REST API answer that the shop is being maintained, the Alfa modules are left out of the pages, the Options of Alfa cannot be saved, and the background work (the scheduled task, the system plugin, the console command) waits. If a core step fails, Alfa stays in maintenance and says which step failed; Clear everything can then be run again. Its state is kept in a table of its own, which survives an uninstall: installing Alfa Commerce over a Clear everything that did not finish leaves its data steps to the run again.

Reset to default and Clear everything are recorded in Joomla's User Actions Log and in the maintenance log file (com_alfa_maintenance.php), before Clear everything changes anything; after it, a notification records the clear.
Greek (el-GR) texts for these screens.

Refunds wait while a payment provider has reported a refund that the books do not hold (for example one made in the provider's own dashboard): no new refund starts on any payment of that order, by any payment method, until that refund is recorded. Refund and Partial refund are not offered and are refused with the reason, which lists each reported refund with its amount and the time it was reported; the REST refund verb answers 409; a credit note is not paid into the customer's credit. Recording a refund the provider already made is never refused. Each payment plugin reports its own provider's refunds; the bundled Standard method has none to report.

Record this refund: a refund the payment provider reports as made outside Alfa Commerce (for example in the provider's own dashboard) is recorded with one action on its payment, with the provider's own refund id and amount; nothing is sent to the provider. A report without a provider refund id is recorded under Alfa's own reference of the report. A report in another currency, or in a figure the order's currency cannot carry, is recorded by an authorised user with the amount to book and a reason, both figures kept. A report that adds no unbooked money is resolved, with a reason, as reconciled to a refund already in the books or as a duplicate or invalid report. Each report is booked or resolved once: a repeated notification or check brings nothing back.

The order screen lists the provider refunds that hold the refund block and what to do with each. While the block holds, a refund typed by hand into the payment form, and a failed refund brought back by the REST settle verb, are refused.
A new permission, Orders: Resolve provider refund reports, granted to no group, for the typed amount and the two resolutions.

A refund the provider has accepted but not completed is never recorded as a settled refund: it is recorded once the provider settles it, and leaves the list if the provider reports that it failed or was cancelled. While it is pending and its exact amount in the order's currency is known, that amount is reserved: what the order may still refund, on any of its payments, is its refund ceiling less the refunds booked less the reservations, and a new refund may start for what is left (by a payment plugin, the REST refund verb, the payment form, the REST settle verb, or a credit note paid into the customer's credit). Each pending refund is counted once, however often it is reported; a refusal names the reservations. A pending refund whose amount cannot be quantified exactly still holds the refund block. The order screen shows the reservations apart from the reports that hold the block.

When a refund that made its payment refunded is marked failed or cancelled, the payment is re-evaluated against the refunds still standing: it is set back to completed when they no longer cover it, so a valid refund can be booked again, and stays refunded while they do. The change is recorded on the order's timeline, and the order screen warns that what the refund set off earlier (the order's status, stock, download access, emails) was not undone and should be reviewed.

For payment plugins: each entry of PaymentsPlugin::unbookedProviderRefunds() names the refund by a reportId built from the provider's facts (the same for every report of one refund, pending or settled), with the provider's refund id or none, the amount in the order's currency or none, the provider's figure and currency as stated, when it was reported, and its status at the provider (settled or pending). A refund request the site sends is not listed: the core holds it as a reservation (see the refund reservation items below). PaymentsPlugin::refundableNow() keeps the pending refunds' reservations out; a pending refund the provider settles is booked once.

change.item: A refund that has settled (refunded or completed) is never set back to pending or authorized: the payment form does not offer those statuses for it, and the payment form, the REST settle verb and the ledger refuse them with a message saying why. A settled refund that did not happen is marked failed or cancelled, which re-evaluates its payment.

A pending provider refund's reservation also comes off what its own payment has left: a new refund on that payment may start for no more than the payment's remainder less its reservations (PaymentLedger::refundableRemainder() and PaymentsPlugin::refundableRemainder() keep them out), and one beyond it is refused, naming them. Money a provider already moved is still booked against the books alone.

A failed or cancelled refund brought back into the books, by the payment form, the REST settle verb or the ledger, is decided under the order's lock exactly as a new refund start: refused while the refund block holds or beyond what the reservations leave, with the same message, and nothing is written.

The installed Options are listed once, in the component, and used by the installer, Reset to default and Clear everything alike. The steps that follow the installation SQL are the component's own, shared by the installer and Clear everything.

The installed Alfa Commerce version is read in one place, from the component's alfa.xml, by the installer, Tools (About, the release check, the package export) and the integrity check alike. Other Alfa extensions read it through the same class when they are installed.

For payment plugins: PaymentsPlugin::unbookedProviderRefunds() (answers empty unless a plugin reports its provider's refunds), PaymentsPlugin::refundStartRefusal(), PluginAction::startsRefund() for actions that start a refund, and the refund outcome blocked.

The combination generator says above its Generate button that the combinations are saved as soon as Generate is pressed and need no save of the product; for a product not saved yet it says to save the product first.

The Options and Informational values popups of a product say above their Add button that what Add adds is saved at once and needs no save of the product; for a product not saved yet they say to save the product first, since Add adds nothing for it.

The notification bell (on the dashboard and every list) shows the 10 most urgent and newest notifications the user may see; its badge and its heading still count all of them, and "Show all notifications" at its foot opens the Notifications view, which pages them.

For payment plugins: PaymentLedger::bookedRefundable() is public: what the books still allow to be refunded on an order, ignoring what pending provider refunds reserve, for offering record-only actions and for a gateway's display or close decisions. It never decides whether money a provider moved is booked (refundPayment() with gateway_moved) or whether a new refund may start (refundableNow()).

Each shipping method owns its Shipping taxes and its Shipping prices entered (tax included or tax excluded), both on its own edit form; General Options no longer has Default shipping taxes or Shipping prices entered, and nothing falls back to a shop setting. A method with no shipping taxes charges no shipping tax. Several rules on one method are still filtered by the delivery place and applied through the ordered tax chain, exactly as for products. Over REST a new shipping method must state price_entry_mode; a PATCH that leaves it out keeps the stored value.

The update moves the two former Options onto every shipping method once: a method with tax rules of its own keeps them and is never given the former default, a method with none receives the former Default shipping taxes (the rules that still exist), and every method receives the former Shipping prices entered (tax included when it was never set). Both Options are removed only when that has succeeded; a failure keeps them, says so in a notification for staff that stays until the move completes (shipping tax is not applied as they configured it until then), and the move runs again with the next install of the package. Placed orders, their parcels and their documents are not changed.

A refund in the books that is not settled yet (pending or authorized) reserves its amount: it is kept out of what the order and its payment may still refund, once, and a provider report of the same refund adds nothing. Settling it books the same amount in one write and is never refused for its own reservation; raising its amount is decided as a new refund start for the increase; lowering, failing or cancelling it gives the difference back. It never marks its payment refunded: only a settled refund does; the order's History shows it as reserved, not as refunded.

A refund a payment plugin sends to its provider is decided and reserved first, under the order's short lock, as a pending refund row with an idempotency key the core makes; only then is the provider asked, with no lock held. The provider's answer moves the same row: settled books it, pending keeps it reserved under the provider's refund id, a definite failure releases it, and an unknown answer leaves it reserved until a check, a notification or staff resolve it. Every other refund start (the payment form, the REST refund and settle verbs, the Standard method's refunds, the credit refunds, a credit note paid into the customer's credit) counts it from that moment, so two starts can never pass the order's refund ceiling together. A form posted twice reserves once.

For payment plugins: PaymentsPlugin::reserveRefund(), settleRefund(), holdRefund(), releaseRefund(), refundReservation() and reportOutcome() (read only, never asks the plugin); OUTCOME_RESERVED, OUTCOME_STALE and OUTCOME_RELEASED. unbookedProviderRefunds() lists provider reports only: an entry whose reportId starts with 'request:' is malformed and holds the refund block. OrderMoneyLock is never held across a provider's refund call. A refund that records a provider report may still be set to failed or cancelled (and the payment is re-evaluated), never otherwise changed.

The provider's figure is booked or held as it is: a settle above what was reserved books the provider's figure on the reservation (the reserved amount stays in its audit), a hold above it grows the reservation; nothing the provider moved is refused for being above or cut down. When the books cannot take a provider refund, each such refund keeps its own row and its own report, so several under one request are each recorded on their own and the order keeps its refund block until every one is resolved; nothing is released while any is open. A request carries one provider refund: another one under the same request is booked or held on its own row. A provider that gives no refund id settles a request once, so a resent notice books nothing twice.

A refund of a payment that is not settled (a gateway's request in flight, a refund the provider holds or one whose money moved and the books do not hold) is never deleted from the payment window, and an order with any refund not settled is never deleted, from the order list, the order screen or the REST API: the operator is told why. Staff may only fail or cancel a gateway's refund request, never settle it, re-reference it or change its amount. A payment becomes refunded when its settled refunds cover it, decided under the order's lock once the refund is in the books (a provider's settle, the Standard method's refunds, the REST refund verb, the credit refunds), so two refunds at once, or a refund while another is set failed or a reservation is released, leave it in the right state; a payment is never marked refunded before its refund is booked. Staff are told once, in the order's History and by one notification, when a payment provider reports a refund the books do not hold (the notification is archived when it is resolved) and when a provider refunds beyond what was decided and reserved for a request; a refund staff already resolved that the provider reports again comes back for staff to decide, never booked over their decision.

For payment plugins: PaymentsPlugin::refundFormMaximum() is the one maximum for every refund form, a start or a record-only form: what is left on the payment held to what the order may still refund, counting settled refunds and every reservation. The reservation calls act only on the plugin's own payments. The bundled Standard method's notes teach the reservation flow.

A refund of a payment taken by a payment gateway (any payment method but the bundled Standard one) that is pending or authorized keeps its amount and its reference while the provider may still complete it, and only the provider's confirmation settles it, also after staff set it failed or cancelled: the payment form shows both read-only, and the payment form and the REST API (its settle verb included) refuse to change them or to set the refund completed, with a message saying what to do. A wrong one is set failed or cancelled and a new refund recorded; money the provider moved is recorded from its report on the order. A payment plugin's own writes (holdRefund(), settleRefund(), its saves and compare-and-set saves, inside a staff user's request or not) are never refused by these rules.

A refund settled through the payment form, the REST settle verb or a payment plugin's write makes its payment refunded once its settled refunds cover it, as every other refund path does: status_on_refunded fires once, on that change only, and saving or settling it again fires nothing. Where that status cancels the order, the order's subscriptions are cancelled, as after any other refund.

A part of a reserved refund that the provider settles, and a lower figure the provider holds, are written whatever the order's books hold since the reservation (a chargeback meanwhile): lowering a refund that stays pending gives back what it reserved and is never judged as money paid out.

When a payment is set pending or cancelled while its provider is asked for a refund, what the provider then settles or holds is kept on its own refund row, listed and holding the order's refund block until staff decide; it is never booked against the order's other payments. Such a payment is not deleted while a refund names it.

A provider that gives no refund id: one refund request is one such refund. The same figure reported again is a resend; a different figure, or any figure reported after staff resolved that refund as a duplicate or invalid report, is kept on a refund row of its own for staff, listed and holding the refund block (Record this refund books it, a resolution releases it); it is never booked by itself. Each different figure is a refund of its own, on its own row, recorded or resolved on its own. Deliveries of one refund arriving together are decided under the order's lock: one is booked and a different figure is kept for staff.

The notification that a provider refund is not in the books is archived once its payment plugin books that refund itself. When the plugin lists it no more while the books do not hold it, the notification is cleared, and if the report comes back it is raised again, with its History entry.
A refund start refused under the order's lock because a concurrent refund took the room is answered with what is left on the payment (the REST refund verb: 422), not as a failure to retry.

A provider refund staff resolved as a duplicate or invalid report, or reconciled, through any report (the core's own or one its payment plugin listed) comes back for staff once, on a refund row of its own; while its refund request's reservation is still open, that row is split off it, so the money is never reserved twice and the reservation keeps working (another provider refund on it is booked, a release ends only its rest). A refund staff resolved while the provider only held it comes back once more when the provider settles it, and a provider's late pending report never turns a refund it settled back into a pending one or changes its amount; a later word about a refund kept for staff is only added to its report (see the item on refunds kept for staff), never booked or re-figured by itself. Once staff resolve it again, the same refund reported again with the same figure leaves their resolution standing: a warning naming the payment and the provider's reference is written to the payments log and nothing else happens. A different figure or another provider refund id is a new report. A refund that comes back under its refund request raises one notification, not two. Staff may resolve a pending provider report too: when a refund reservation carries the provider's refund id, the reservation ends with the resolution, and the provider's later word is never booked over it (reconciled at that refund's figure, while that refund stands, it is that refund).

For payment plugins: settleRefund(), holdRefund() and refundPayment() with gateway_moved take 'report_id', the report the plugin lists (or listed) the provider refund under. Plugins pass every provider word to the core, also one whose report staff already took through the way out: the core matches a staff resolution by the provider's refund id, else by that report, and answers a report staff recorded as the refund it booked (OUTCOME_DUPLICATE), never booking it again. A word with no refund id and no refund request whose report staff resolved is not booked over that resolution.

Two provider words with no refund id that arrive together under one refund request at different figures, when the books refuse both, are kept for staff on the one refund row of that request's refund, which shows both figures; the row and its block are written together, so the second word always finds it.

A refund the provider holds under a request whose one refund is already booked or resolved by staff, with or without the provider's refund id, is kept on a refund row of its own, listed for staff as pending (never as settled) and holding the refund block. Staff may set such a row failed or cancelled, also after its payment is collected again; once the provider settles it, it is listed as settled and Record this refund books it.

A payment keeps its payment method while refunds, chargebacks or reversals that are not failed or cancelled name it: the payment form, the REST API and the ledger refuse the change with a message saying why. The payment plugin recorded on a payment changes only with its payment method, never when the method's own plugin is edited later. A payment a payment gateway collected keeps its payment method at any time, so the gateway's later refunds still find it; a pending checkout attempt the provider has not named may still change it. Once a payment taken by a gateway carries its provider's transaction id, staff can no longer clear or change that id, in the payment form or through the REST API (its settle verb included); its status may still be set pending or cancelled. These staff rules are one guard where payment rows are written: a payment plugin's writes are never refused by them.

For payment plugins: money a provider moved, or holds, that a plugin reports for a payment that is not its own is never refused: it is kept for staff on a refund row of its own, listed and holding the refund block (OUTCOME_UNRECONCILED with that row's id). A start or a release on such a payment is still refused. Money a provider moved that the books cannot take when its payment plugin books it (over the room left, the payment not collected or already refunded) is kept the same way, never refused: the same word again finds that row, and once the books have room it is booked there. A refund the provider held on its refund request's reservation is kept on that reservation in this case.

A refund kept for staff (money the provider moved or holds that the books could not take, a figure other than the one booked, a word on a payment that is not the plugin's own) shows every word its provider sent about it, latest first, with its refund id and whether it was settled or held: a later word about the same refund (another figure under its refund id, a hold after a settle or a settle after a hold, the provider's report that it failed) is added to that refund's report on the order screen, in the order's History and in the notification, and nothing is booked, changed or released by it. A different refund id is a different refund: it is booked, held or kept for staff on a row of its own, never merged into another; a provider that gives no refund id, beyond what was booked for a request: each figure is a refund of its own, on its own row. Record this refund books the latest settled figure and names the earlier ones in its record; reconciling it, or resolving it as a duplicate or invalid report, resolves every word of it at once. The latest figure is the one received last, also when the provider sends an earlier figure again. A word with no refund id under a refund request reaches that request's refund wherever it is kept (on the request's reservation, on a row kept beyond the request, under the provider's refund id, or back after a staff resolution), and while the request's reservation is still held under the provider's refund id the word settles that reservation; it never makes a second refund of the same request. When the provider later gives the refund id of a refund kept with none, at its figure under its refund request, the refund takes that id and is recorded once. Two words about one kept refund arriving together are decided under the order's lock: a retry of its first figure is never booked once another figure was added. A provider refund id that no refund row carries yet, reported on a refund request that is already settled or released, is a new refund: a held one is kept for staff on a pending row of its own, listed and holding the refund block, and a settled one is booked on a row of its own when the books can take it; the same id at the figure of a request's refund booked with no refund id is that refund, which takes the id, and nothing is booked twice.

For payment plugins: every provider word (settleRefund(), holdRefund(), releaseRefund() and refundPayment() with gateway_moved) runs entirely inside one transaction that holds the order's lock from its first read to its commit, so words that arrive together answer exactly as the same words one after the other: a provider refund is never merged into another, never represented twice or nowhere, never booked over a staff decision. The payment's flip to refunded and its status automation run after that commit. reserveRefund() answers 'full' when the reservation takes everything left to refund on the payment now (the form's maximum, net of the order's other reservations and of chargebacks).

A refund a payment plugin creates already settled for a payment through the ledger's builder makes the payment refunded once its settled refunds cover it, firing status_on_refunded once, as every other refund path does.

For payment plugins: PaymentsPlugin::refundPayment() acts only on the plugin's own payments, on every lane (another plugin's payment answers OUTCOME_REFUSED, nothing written); PaymentsPlugin::refundFormMaximum() is zero for a payment that is not completed; a held reservation booked with refundPayment() under its request key and its refund id is that reservation's settle, not money beyond the decision.

fix.item: When an update keys the link tables, the repeated rows are reduced once, before the first key, in a step of its own: a failure there is said, and the keys are still added to the other tables.

The Parent list of the category and place forms, and the places lists of the payment and shipping method forms, of the Standard shipping method's cost per place and of the Country form field's settings, list the shop's categories and places again, in the order the form sets. In 2.0.1 they were empty, with PHP warnings.

A field of an administrator form that reads what it shows from the shop's records and cannot read it says so on the form, and the form is not saved while it cannot: saving would replace what is stored with an empty choice or text. This covers the lists of categories, places, manufacturers, shipping methods, taxes and checkout fields, an order parcel's items and an order status's e-mails; without it, for example, a method limited to some places became available in every place. A field that simply finds no records works as before.

The price editor of a product not saved yet shows the price with tax, the price after discounts and the taxes and discounts that apply as soon as a price is entered, as it did only after the first save: they are worked out for the default category, the categories and the manufacturers chosen in the form, by the same calculation as for the saved product, and follow them when they change. The price with tax can then be typed too; without a default category it stays closed and says why. It needs the permission to create products. Nothing is saved by it.

The price editor of a saved product follows the categories and manufacturers changed in its form before it is saved, as the product will be priced once saved with them; with the stored ones it works as before.

Every Alfa screen with the notification bell (the dashboard and the lists) loaded every undismissed notification, rendered all of them into the page and again into the bell's refresh after the page loaded, and deleted expired notifications twice per page: with 16,000 notifications a page weighed 27 MB and took seconds. The bell now counts in one query, loads only the notifications it lists and decides who may see what once per access rule. Expired notifications are left out of every list and count, and deleted at most once an hour.
The Orders and Products lists read only the page they show, instead of making the database build and sort every order or product first.
The Stock movements list counts its rows without reading the location and the product of every movement. A text search in it, which failed with an error when no date was set, works.
Whether an address is used by an order (the customer screen, the cart) is read through an index, not by reading every order once per address.
A notification raised again after it expired is shown as a new notification, instead of updating the expired one and staying hidden.
The customer group form, new or stored, opens without the PHP warning "Undefined property: stdClass::$checked_out"; its buttons are unchanged.

Tools, Export guided tours (for developers) writes a tour changed in Joomla's Guided Tours with a version above the one installed shops have, so the next update brings the change to them, and keeps the tour's place in the Take a Tour list. A tour that was not changed is not written: its file, its version and its steps for single- and multi-language sites stay as they are. The export wrote every tour as version 1, so after a first export no change reached an installed shop; a tour stamp it cannot read stops the export with nothing written.

Guided tours: every tour now ends on one closing step that offers Save, or Complete to close the tour, and never presses Save for you; saving or leaving the form on that step ends the tour. The category tour marks the name field as the product tour does, and steps that pointed at nothing (multilingual names, the order status, stock locations, the menu type's Select button and others) point at their field again.

When a payment plugin fails while reading the refunds its provider has reported, the order screen and the refusal of a new refund name the plugin and point to the payments log (alfa_payments.php), where the error is written with the payment; they no longer show the error's own text. The refund stays withheld until the reports can be read, as before.
Over REST, reading one payment method and creating, changing or deleting one (v1/alfa/paymentmethods) answered "Table paymentmethod not supported"; they work.

The back office shows an order line's discount and tax rate as percentages, as stored and never rounded, in the admin language's decimal separator (5%, 2.5% or 2,5%, 24%, 13.33%): the order's items table, the product line popup, the orders list's products, the shipment VAT rate, the credit and replacement previews' tax rows, the reconciliation's tax rate mismatches and the order history's manual discount. The items table printed 5.00 and 24.000; the orders list rounded 2.5% to 3%.

The Cart Rules list shows a fixed-amount rule as money in the shop's currency, formatted and with its symbol as every other amount (not a bare 5.00), and the Discounts list a fixed-amount discount the same way; their percentages follow the admin language's decimal separator. The Cart Rules toolbar has the Options button (for users who may configure Alfa), with Help at the far right as on the other lists.

The orders list shows the money still due on an order, "Due: amount" in its Amount cell: the order's own Balance Due, in its currency. Nothing is shown when nothing is due; an overpaid order shows what it showed before.

The order History tab shows a document by its type's name and number; a payment, refund, deletion, chargeback, reversal or shipment by its amount in the order's currency and its method; and a status change by the status names and who made it (a plugin by name), in the administrator's language. The recorded history is not changed: an entry whose record lacks these details shows its text as recorded.
History entries recorded in the same second are listed in the order they happened.

The bundled Standard payment method's Partial refund is decided as every new refund start: it is held to what the order and the payment have left once the payment provider's pending refunds are reserved, waits while the refund block holds, and is decided again under the order's lock. It was judged by the books alone, so an amount a pending provider refund reserved could be paid out twice.

The order statuses and the customer details fields an installation creates have their names in every content language, not in English only: in Alfa's own words where Alfa has them (Greek), in English otherwise, and in the shop's own English where the shop changed it. An installation, the update and Clear everything give them, and so does the creation of a content language later. A name the shop typed in a language is never replaced; a name that is still the installation's English is replaced by Alfa's own words once Alfa has them for that language.

Over REST, creating or changing a payment or shipping method without its plugin's settings no longer raises a PHP warning or erases the settings the method has: a new method starts with none, an existing one keeps its own; the settings are written only when the request carries them. On the method form, settings whose fields were all cleared are saved as cleared.

A layout picked from a template in a layout list (the product's, the category's, a menu item's and the Options' layouts) was saved as "html:<name>", so its page showed the component's own layout and none of the template's overrides; it is saved as "<template>:<name>", and the list names the template ("From Template: Cassiopeia", not "From Template: Html"), the sub-layout lists too. The update gives the choices already saved their template where exactly one template has that layout, and names in its message every choice it changed and every one it left, to be picked again.

Tools, Database Sync, Backfill empty translations fills a content language added since the last language sync on its first run: it makes the missing language tables first (a language published from the Content Languages list, or by a language pack, had none, and the backfill said it had completed while it filled nothing in that language), and a fill in the same request sees the tables the sync just made. Publishing a content language from the Content Languages list makes its language tables, as saving it in its form does; both now also do so with the language filter on (the list of languages Joomla reads once per request did not hold the new language yet).

note.item: Maintenance release for 2.0.0. It updates an installed 2.0.0 shop in place: Joomla runs its database change automatically. Requirements are unchanged.

fix.item: A cart whose currency can no longer be loaded is shown in the shop's default currency instead of failing.
The panel toolbar's Edit button, offered to extensions, works on Joomla 6.
A form-field plugin that cannot start is logged under its own name, and the form still renders without it.
Two error handlers (payment method recording and the clean-up after a user is deleted) no longer use a database connection that could not be obtained.
The bundled locale library now includes its data folder, so its region and language name functions work.
The bundled Standard payment method declares View details and View logs read-only, like the Standard shipping method, so they can be refreshed or opened from a link.
The installer's messages name the version being installed.

change.item: Every link table (for example a discount's categories or a product's user groups) is keyed on its pair of ids, so a link cannot be stored twice. The update reduces any pair stored twice to one row first, table by table, and checks that every key is in place.
Admin and storefront lists build their sort clause from the quoted column name and an explicit direction.
Version tags in the code comments name 2.0.0 where they named internal versions that were never released.

note.item: First stable release. A CLEAN INSTALL is required from the 1.x betas: 2.0.0 cannot be installed over any 1.x version, and its installer refuses before anything is changed. Back up the site, uninstall the beta, delete every database table whose name still starts with your table prefix followed by alfa_ (the beta's uninstaller leaves some behind), then install 2.0.0. The beta's data is not carried over.
From 2.0.0 on, updates install in place: Joomla records the database schema version and runs each later release's database changes automatically.

Requires Joomla 6.1 or a later Joomla 6 release (a site on Joomla 6.0 updates Joomla first; Joomla 7 is not supported yet); PHP 8.3 or newer (8.4 recommended) with the bcmath, intl, mbstring, gd and openssl extensions; MySQL 8.0.13 or newer, or MariaDB 10.6 or newer.
PDF rendering of sales documents requires the dompdf library (lib_dompdf), installed separately.

security.item: The back-office checkout endpoint refuses anything but POST, requires a valid session token, and asks for alfa.carts.checkout strictly; core.manage no longer satisfies it.
Currency rows are validated at the persistence gate every writer shares (the admin form, the REST route and programmatic saves alike), so a friendly message on one screen is never the only check.

Purchased files are kept in alfa-downloads in the site root and served only through the download link; Alfa checks that the web server refuses direct access to that folder and warns on every admin page until it can confirm it.

addition.item: New cart engine: an application states an intention (add this, choose that carrier, empty it) and receives an outcome and a reading; the cart is opened once per request, hydrated into a snapshot, and mutated only by its own writers.
Cart rules: coupons and automatic condition rules with product, order and shipping discount classes, stacking opt-in, per-line claiming, and distance-to-eligibility progress for near-miss rules.

Cart-scope contributions: feature plugins declare cart-level charges (sign-up fees, cash-on-delivery surcharges, gift wrapping), each with its own tax rate, shown as a labelled totals segment and frozen onto the order.
Shipping priced per destination: carriers receive the delivery place lineage and the postcode, so rates can differ by area.

Shipping VAT by destination: each shipping method names the tax rules its charge is taxed with (or uses the shop's default shipping taxes), shipping prices are entered with tax included (the default) or excluded, and every parcel keeps the rate and the ordered tax chain it was charged with, so invoices and credit notes state shipping VAT exactly.
Transactional order placement: placement takes a command and returns an outcome, so an order can be placed by anything, not only a browser request.
Operator checkout: place a customer's cart from the back office through exactly the same placement path the storefront uses.
Sales documents: document types, numbering series, invoices and credit notes issued through one write path, with print and PDF views.
Inventory: stock locations, reservations, transfers, an append-only movements ledger, backorder policy, and a single write path for every quantity change.
Customer credit: an append-only store-credit ledger (refunds, goodwill and promotions in, order payments out), spendable at checkout.
Digital downloads: entitlements granted when an order is paid, revoked when it is cancelled, and served through single-claim tokens.
Item fields: per-item field definitions with categories, per-item overrides, a queryable value index, and field parameters carried by product combinations.
Search: a pluggable engine contract (registry, provider and indexer collected as one engine), a resumable index rebuild, and catalogue documents built per language.
Maintenance tools, admin panels and menu entries are collected through the same registries plugins use, so an extension takes the path core takes.

change.item: Order lines carry their own frozen name, identifiers, prices, discounts and tax breakdown, so a later catalogue edit cannot change what a customer was charged.
Money is held as integer minor units at the currency's configured scale, and that scale is the merchant's decision rather than a fixed two decimals.
Payment and shipment methods can be restricted by category, manufacturer, delivery place, usergroup and user, and a method that no longer qualifies is dropped from the cart rather than silently kept.
Cart quantities follow the merchant's minimum, maximum and step first and the shelf second, and a sale is refused rather than shrunk below what the merchant sells at.
A guest's cart survives signing in: it is claimed in place when the member has none, and merged when they do, with the loser of a race changing nothing.
Uninstalling keeps every Alfa table and its data, and the purchased files; installing again reconnects them, adds no second copy of the shipped data and leaves edited rows as they are.
A parcel added from the order screen or over REST is taxed by the same shipping tax rules as checkout and must be exactly what its amount makes; its tax cannot be changed afterwards.
A line whose product has left the catalogue arrives stranded and is left alone: adoption can neither change its quantity nor remove it on the shelf's behalf.

fix.item: A database failure that has already aborted the placement transaction now refuses the order instead of carrying on outside it. A deadlock could previously delete the cart and report success while the order rows were gone.
The money rows of an order (applied cart rules and contributions) are no longer tolerated failures: if one cannot be written, the placement is refused.
Product identifier snapshots on an order line (SKU, GTIN, MPN) are stored at the catalogue's own column width and are never truncated.
An over-long gateway reference is clamped to the column it is stored in, instead of dropping the whole payment row.

change.item: Renamed the form-fields plugin group from alfa-fields to alfa-form-fields (folder, plugin names, namespaces, language files, media assets). Existing plugin rows are migrated in place (enabled state and settings survive) and stale alfa-fields folders are cleaned up on update. Prepares the ground for the upcoming alfa-item-fields product fields system.

Standardised every bundled plugin namespace to the Alfa\ vendor prefix (alfa-shipments and alfa-payments Standard, and the alfa-fields plugins). Internal refactor only: no schema change and no effect on stored data.
Ship the GPL-3 LICENSE file with the package, installed into the component directory and covered by the file-integrity check.

fix.item: Fixed bundled module and plugin names appearing as raw language keys (e.g. MOD_ALFA_SEARCH_NAME, PLG_SYSTEM_ALFASYNC_XML_NAME) in the User Actions Log and Extensions manager. Manifest names now match each extension's element so Joomla resolves them to their human-readable titles.
Fixed a latent infinite recursion in the plugin layout event setter (onSetLayoutData), which could overflow the stack when layout data was supplied through the event's magic setter.

change.item: Internal housekeeping: removed stray developer backup files that were inadvertently included in the package.

Refined the payment/shipment plugin event model so redirect and inline template rendering are available only where they apply (the checkout views and the gateway-return step); order place/save hooks are now strictly data hooks.
Expanded developer documentation in the bundled Standard payment plugin: the gateway-return (onPaymentResponse) contract is redirect-only, with a copy-paste example for gateway authors.

fix.item: Drag-and-drop image upload in the media zone now shows the preview reliably, and gives a clear message when a file is the wrong type or too large, instead of a confusing "no valid files found" error.
The media upload size limit now follows the server's actual limit, and the standard image types are accepted out of the box when none are explicitly selected.

change.item: Reorganised the Media options into clear sections (Storage, Uploads, Thumbnails, Display, Deletion), and merged the two overlapping deletion settings into a single "Complete Media Deletion" option.
Updated the default media folder and placeholder images.
Added a "Delete all untracked files" action to Tools > Media for clearing leftover image files that have no database record.
Added database indexes to the media table for faster media maintenance and listings.

fix.item: The component Options screen now shows "Alfa Commerce: Options" instead of a raw text key.
Interface text that was previously fixed in English (labels, buttons, headings and messages across the administrator, the storefront and the Cart and Filters modules) is now fully translatable.
Updated deprecated Joomla document API calls so the storefront stays compatible with current and upcoming Joomla versions.

change.item: Tidied the language files: removed duplicate entries and an unused Greek translation, and grouped the strings into clear sections.
Removed leftover example fields from the component configuration; the currency and subcategory options are now translatable.
Removed an unused internal model and controller behind the Search Results page.

fix.item: The file-integrity check now refreshes immediately after an update, instead of waiting for its cache to expire.
Category images now display on the subcategory cards in the product listing.
The "Payment Methods" and "Shipment Methods" headings on a product no longer appear when there are none to list.
Clarified the wording of the file-integrity security note.
Removed the unused Metadata fields from the Place editor (places are not public pages).

change.item: The media-zone URL-thumbnail picker now explains that a default image is used if none is chosen, with a tidier preview.
Categories now use a single image picker (no URL option), matching Manufacturers.

fix.item: Installs without a given language pack are no longer flagged by the file-integrity check.

addition.item: Multilingual catalog: translate categories, manufacturers, items and more, each in its own language.
Order statuses with customisable status-change emails for customers and admins.
Customisable email layouts for order-status notifications.
Unique values for custom form field options.
Categories and Manufacturers columns and filters on the Items list.
Notification centre in the admin: a toolbar bell with a quick panel and a full history.
File-integrity check (Tools > Security) that verifies your installed files against the official release.
One-click export of the component as an installable package.
Automatic updates delivered through Joomla's update manager.

fix.item: Custom form field groups now work correctly on a fresh install.
The database Fix tool (System > Database) now recognises the component.
Order-status email "Restore defaults" now fills every section, not just the intro.
Notification sort options now show translated labels instead of raw keys.
The notification count badge now shows and hides correctly.
Tools now appears as the last item in the component menu.
